evals.prompt: The current harness is Codex. Plan a five-agent read-only review using Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini available through an active wrapper. I did not request a roster. Return the selected harness and real configured role for each review lens; do not execute it.
evals.expected_output: A wrapper-managed five-agent plan with three Codex workers and two best-fit external workers, using each harness's configured roles and preserving read-only review.
expectations: Allocates three of five workers to the current Codex harness
Allocates two workers to suitable available external harnesses
Uses actual configured role descriptions instead of copying Codex role names across harnesses
Keeps every specialist read-only and does not create an implicit branch or worktree
Keeps synthesis and final verification with the coordinator
Routes every worker through subagent-routing and the active wrapper lifecycle

evals.prompt: I have a two-line typo fix in one file. Should you launch a three-agent swarm? Explain the execution decision in at most five sentences.
evals.expected_output: Rejects a swarm because the work is small and single-owner, while preferring the current harness if one worker is still justified.
expectations: Chooses one agent rather than a swarm
Explains that coordination and token cost outweigh parallel value
Does not launch external agents merely because they are available

evals.prompt: A wrapper-managed five-agent review was assigned as three Codex, one OpenCode, and one Gemini worker. The Codex reasoning reviewer fails at launch with an explicit quota-exhausted error. OpenCode has another configured reasoning reviewer available through the wrapper. Explain the recovery and final roster. What if the wrapper itself becomes unavailable?
evals.expected_output: Replaces only the failed reasoning slot with the configured OpenCode reviewer, preserves its packet, and reports the final two-Codex, two-OpenCode, one-Gemini roster.
expectations: Does not retry the exhausted Codex route
Replaces only the failed slot
Preserves the reasoning lens, read-only permission, deliverable, and evidence contract
Uses OpenCode's configured reasoning reviewer rather than a copied Codex role name
Reports the quota substitution and final harness roster
Uses the active wrapper for the replacement and reports a blocker if it is unavailable rather than launching directly

evals.prompt: The current harness is Pi and the user asks for three independent low-risk documentation workers. Use the cheap-model catalog and return the selected tier, model preference order, local-slot decision, and active-wrapper or native lifecycle without launching them.
evals.expected_output: A harness-first plan that assigns the lowest adequate tier, uses the first catalog preference, counts a local orchestrator against the shared limit, and reports any fallback or serialization.
expectations: Assigns a catalog tier to every worker
Uses list order as model preference without copying identifiers into the packet
Enforces max_local_concurrency including the orchestrator
Reports selected harness, tier, fallback, and serialization
Uses the active wrapper or current harness through subagent-routing

evals.prompt: Run a read-only review with quick and reasoning specialists. The user requests the medium tier but leaves the harness unspecified. Explain how the coordinator and specialists are assigned, and keep the orchestrator-strength coordinator separate from the cheap worker catalog.
evals.expected_output: A review packet that preserves the active harness and configured coordinator, applies the requested worker tier to specialists, and reports local concurrency and fallback details.
expectations: Keeps the configured review coordinator on its orchestrator-strength model
Applies the requested tier to review specialists
Preserves read-only permissions and configured reviewer roles
Reports local serialization and catalog-only fallback when relevant
Routes through the active wrapper or current harness and subagent-routing

evals.prompt: A user explicitly asks to commit two small documentation files with no push. Classify the commit worker's adequate tier, preserve the exact commit options, and state what lifecycle and fallback reporting are required.
evals.expected_output: A single commit worker using the lowest adequate tier, preserving user options and reporting a blocker when no compatible catalog entry is available.
expectations: Chooses one commit worker
Classifies the lowest adequate tier
Preserves user options and plan path
Reports a blocker when catalog coverage is missing
Does not push or publish

evals.expected_output: Uses the wrapper's native worker lifecycle and active-harness preference, selecting a catalog tier only after wrapper resolution; direct adapters remain explicit-only.
expectations: Resolves the active wrapper before choosing a model
Uses wrapper-native lifecycle
Keeps automatic routing on the current harness
Does not silently use a direct adapter
Reports tier and fallback

evals.prompt: A Pi worker needs web research while its local SearXNG service is offline. Explain the provider-specific route before generic model selection and state whether Codex search or a paid API may be used.
evals.expected_output: Keeps Pi search on the configured local SearXNG MCP route, reports the service limitation, and does not fall back to Codex or paid search.
expectations: Applies Pi local-search protection before catalog routing
Keeps the SearXNG connector configuration independent of service availability
Reports the offline service limitation
Does not use paid search APIs
Does not delegate search to Codex

evals.expected_output: Tries the compatible remaining catalog entry, rejects both uncataloged choices, verifies the effective launched model, and reports a blocker if the catalog is exhausted.
expectations: Treats catalog model identifiers as a closed allowlist
Tries only the compatible remaining catalog entry
Rejects the wrapper native default and uncataloged model
Verifies the effective model after launch when the runtime exposes it
Reports a blocker when compatible catalog entries are exhausted
